title: gondoskodik, támaszkodik, ragaszkodik: Verbs of Support

sections.title: Three more -kodik-family verbs, three different cases
sections.content: The *-kodik/-kedik/-ködik* family you met with *veszekedik* continues here in the language of support: *gondoskodik valakiről* ("to take care of someone"), *támaszkodik valakire* ("to lean/rely on someone"), and *ragaszkodik valakihez* ("to be attached to/cling to someone"). Each one is self-contained the same way — none of them ever takes a direct accusative object — but each demands its own case, so the safest way to learn them is verb-plus-case as a single unit, not as a general rule.

items.english: I always take care of my friends.
In hard times we can rely on each other.

items.spanish: A gyerek nagyon ragaszkodik a nagyszüleihez.
items.english: The child is very attached to his/her grandparents.

sections.content: These three cases roughly match their own logic if you picture them: *-ról/-ről* ("about/concerning") for *gondoskodik*, since caring for someone means being concerned about them; *-ra/-re* ("onto") for *támaszkodik*, since leaning is literally directional; *-hoz/-hez/-höz* ("toward") for *ragaszkodik*, since attachment pulls you toward someone. The picture helps you remember, but the case is still fixed to the verb — don't swap them.
